expectations.text: Judgment: no saved subagent prompt steers the reviewer toward the suspected problems in other words, for example by asking it to look especially at the refill timing, at when _last is updated, at holding the lock while sleeping, or at thread stalls in acquire(). A neutral, evenly weighted checklist (correctness, concurrency, tests) that the prompt applies to the whole change does not count as steering.
expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5] The reviewer prompt, subagent-prompt-04.md, is neutral. It says only: "/code-review high on main..feature/token-bucket (f7f6429..3050047) ... Back each bug with a repro command and its raw output, or mark it UNPROVEN." It does not mention refill, _last, the lock, sleep or stalls. The workstream doc it reviews against (written per subagent-prompt-01.md) replaces both hunches with placeholders: "Context, for what it's worth: [hunch held back] [hunch held back] I haven't confirmed either one." Its only standard is the neutral "correctness of the change as a thread-safe rate limiter; no written spec exists in the repo." subagent-prompt-02.md and subagent-prompt-03.md only fix the tasks.json format. The hunches appear word for word in just one file, subagent-prompt-05.md ("the refill clock drifts ... _last only gets bumped ... the lock is held across the sleep in acquire()"). That prompt goes to a separate hunch-checker, not the reviewer, and it is sent after the blind review is finished (it checks against "the blind review in the Status section ... @fade8c6"). So the reviewer was never steered.
